chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the miscarried fetus: when its creation is complete, do ghusl, lahd, and shrouding become obligatory for it? He said: “Yes, all of that becomes obligatory for it when it is complete.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: The muhrim, when he dies, is washed, shrouded, and his face is covered with the shroud, except that camphor and other perfume are not brought near him, and there is no tahnit for him.

key_terms.اللَّحْدُ: the burial niche in the grave
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: a person in the state of ihram
key_terms.تَحْنِيطٌ: anointing the deceased with camphor or funeral scenting

ai.seo_question: What are the funeral rulings for a fully formed miscarried fetus and for a muhrim who dies?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings concerning funeral rites. It states that when a miscarried fetus has fully formed features, ghusl, burial preparation, and shrouding are obligatory for it; it also states that a deceased muhrim is washed and shrouded, but no camphor, perfume, or tahnit is used for him.
